evidence.field: description, source attribution, original file link, reuse rights and upload history
evidence.text: The exact file page identifies 比-seal.svg as a modern vector drawing of 比 in Shuowen seal-script style, links the model to image s05946 on 比’s Hanziyuan page, and offers an original SVG link. Commons marks the representation public domain; its file history dates the upload to 8 August 2009. This illustrates a labeled seal-script form, not an ancient artifact or settled graph analysis.
evidence.title: File:比-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.field: description, source attribution, original file link, reuse rights and upload history
evidence.text: The exact file page identifies 比-oracle.svg as a modern vector drawing labeled Shang oracle-script style, links the model to image j19532 on 比’s Hanziyuan page, and offers an original SVG link. Commons marks the representation public domain; its file history dates the upload to 8 August 2009. The page also categorizes it as containing oracle-匕, which is project metadata and does not independently prove the early sign’s referent or settle the disputed formation analysis.
evidence.title: File:比-oracle.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.source: Wikimedia Commons, Ancient Chinese characters/Richard Sears Agreement
evidence.text: Commons states that the copyright holder approved publication of the referenced character images and records the permission correspondence. Its note says the ancient images themselves are public domain and identifies the source collections Sears reported using for seal, bronze, and oracle forms. This is background to the Commons permission provenance; each selected SVG remains a modern vector representation.
evidence.title: Commons:Ancient Chinese characters/Richard Sears Agreement

evidence.field: Old Chinese and Middle Chinese reconstruction entries
evidence.text: The 2014 Baxter–Sagart table distinguishes 比 bǐ, MC pjijX, OC *C.pijʔ, gloss ‘compare’, from 比 bì, MC pjijH, OC *pij-s, gloss ‘combine; all’. It lists 匕 bǐ, MC pjijX, OC *pijʔ, gloss ‘ladle, spoon’ and ‘spoon’. These readings resemble each other in this system but do not on their own establish 匕’s role as a sound component in 比.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (13 September 2014)

evidence.source: Local primary reading rows supplied in input; source_path sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt
evidence.field: kMandarin; local rows for 比 and 匕
evidence.text: The supplied local Unihan rows give 比 bǐ and 匕 bǐ. These are current Mandarin metadata, not evidence of an ancient sound relationship. The requested official Unicode click-through pages were attempted but inaccessible in this session.
evidence.title: Unicode Unihan records for 比 (U+6BD4) and 匕 (U+5315)

search_audit.query: 比-seal.svg Wikimedia Commons 比 oracle seal script; 比 oracle bone bronze form 比 字形 小學堂 比 甲骨文
search_audit.outcome: Opened the exact Commons seal file page and attempted both official Unihan pages. Commons page establishes its stated form label, source model, direct original-file link, upload date, and reuse status. Unicode pages returned internal errors.

search_audit.query: site:xiaoxue.iis.sinica.edu.tw/yanbian 比 字形演變 比; Baxter Sagart 2014 比 匕 *C.pijʔ *pijʔ official table
search_audit.outcome: Search did not retrieve an inspectable 比-specific Xiaoxuetang form record. Opened the primary Baxter–Sagart table and inspected entries for 比 and 匕; its notation and distinct readings are preserved.

search_audit.query: exact Commons 比-oracle.svg file page original link and license
search_audit.outcome: Opened the exact oracle file page and Commons agreement. The page supplies the actual original-file URL and rights statement. The image endpoint for the seal version failed with a cache miss; the oracle SVG endpoint was rejected as unsupported content type by the browser. No pixel inspection was performed.

gaps: The browser could not render either direct SVG endpoint, so these are proposed sourced candidates only; image pixels were not visually inspected in this research stage.
No 比-specific Xiaoxuetang record was retrieved or inspected, so no Sinica glyph candidate is proposed.
Official Unicode Unihan pages for 比 and 匕 were inaccessible. The local supplied kMandarin rows were checked, but those rows are not a substitute for verifying the official click-through pages.
Local Baxter–Sagart table rows were supplied for 人, but the external table search did not yield an inspectable 人 entry; no separate external 人 reading is asserted here.

The Commons files are explicitly digital redraws with source-model attribution, not photographs of oracle bones or seal artifacts. Their graphic labels and reuse status do not settle whether the graph depicts people or derives from 匕-like forms.

items.period: Shang (file is labeled Shang oracle-script style; not an artifact date)
items.tradition: Oracle-bone script style; modern vector redraw
items.caption: Modern redraw labeled as 比 in Shang oracle-script style, based on Hanziyuan image j19532. It records one proposed early form; it is not an oracle-bone photograph and does not settle the sign’s origin.
items.alt: A modern vector redraw of a form labeled 比 in Shang oracle-script style.
items.selection_reason: Provides a labeled early-form example relevant to the article’s discussion of disputed early graph analysis; the caption explicitly distinguishes redraw from artifact and avoids asserting the disputed referent.
items.rights: Commons marks the SVG representation public domain; its file page records source-model attribution to Hanziyuan and permission provenance.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style (Han dictionary tradition; the SVG itself was uploaded in 2009)
items.caption: Modern vector drawing of 比 in Shuowen seal-script style, based on Hanziyuan image s05946. It illustrates a later dictionary-form tradition, not an excavated seal inscription.
items.alt: A modern vector redraw of 比 in Shuowen seal-script style.
items.selection_reason: Offers a distinct, explicitly labeled later script-style comparison with the oracle-style redraw while clarifying that both are modern representations.
items.rights: Commons marks the SVG representation public domain; its file page records source-model attribution to Hanziyuan and permission provenance.

limitations.text: Both candidates are modern vector redraws. Their labels and source-model links make them useful as form examples, but neither is a photograph of an ancient artifact or independent evidence for the disputed component analysis. Pixel inspection was not available through the browser.
